description: The figure contains two stacked line plots intended to depict how two quantities related to KV caches evolve over a streaming index \(m\), with both plots sharing the same x-axis labeled \(m\) on a linear scale; the axis begins at 0 on the left and extends rightward with an annotated vertical dashed reference at \(m_0\) (no regular numeric tick labels are shown). In the top plot, the y-axis is labeled \(n\) with a linear scale starting at 0 and annotated horizontal reference levels at \(w\), \(c-a-s\), and \(c-a\); a single black solid line without markers forms a repeating sawtooth pattern: it increases linearly from near 0 up to the dashed level \(c-a\), then drops sharply down to the level \(w\), then rises again in a similar linear ramp to \(c-a\) and repeats, with the sawtooth “teeth” becoming more closely spaced to the right of the vertical dashed line at \(m_0\). In the bottom plot, the y-axis is labeled \(\mathrm{Size}_{run}\) with a linear scale starting at 0 and annotated horizontal reference levels at \(w+a+s\) and \(c\); a single black solid line without markers also forms a repeating sawtooth pattern: it rises linearly from 0 up to the dashed level \(c\), drops sharply down to the dashed level \(w+a+s\), and then repeats the same ramp-and-drop behavior across increasing \(m\), again showing more tightly spaced sawtooth cycles to the right of the vertical dashed line at \(m_0\).
caption_used: The line plots illustrate the evolution of KV caches in the streaming setting, showing variations in two numerical metrics as a function of m. The top plot, with the y-axis labeled n, demonstrates a repeating sawtooth pattern where the values rise linearly to c-a, drop sharply to w, and then stabilize at c-a-s before repeating. The bottom plot, with the y-axis labeled Size_run, similarly exhibits a sawtooth pattern, rising to c, dropping to w+a+s, and then increasing steadily. Notably, the rate of increase in the bottom plot is approximately twice as fast as the top plot, indicating a more rapid growth in Size_run compared to n. Additionally, the m_0 intercept occurs at a higher value in the bottom plot than in the top plot, suggesting a delayed onset of the repeating pattern for Size_run.
